newsitem.title: CHINA: China to crack down on illegal land-use.
newsitem.headline: China to crack down on illegal land-use.

text.p: China is to launch a crackdown on developers who use farmland to build projects such as golf courses and factories to try to cut down on wasteful use of valuable cropland, the China Daily said on Friday.

The State Land Administration would soon send investigators to urge local government agencies to check all cultivated land used for non-agricultural purposes in the past seven years, the newspaper said.
Land approved for non-agricultural projects between January 1 and April 14 this year by local officials who exceeded their authority would be invalid, it said.
"Officials who illegally approve land or dispense with land wastefully... will be held responsible for their wrongdoings," it said.
In urban areas, investigators would check land used by development zones, industrial, commercial and real estate projects, including golf courses, it said.
Developers for many of those projects had left large tracts of land idle or had used land inefficiently, often duplicating construction, it said.
Between 1986 and 1995, about five million hectares (12.4 million acres) of cultivated land was used for non-agricultural projects, it said.
China has tried to cut down on the amount of farmland used for building luxury projects, saying it must feed one-fifth of the world's population on just seven percent of its arable land.
